name: Birdfolk
body:
Birdfolk are free-spirited avian humanoids native to high-mountain ranges and deep canyonlands. Although they are wary of strangers, if approached with caution they may be convinced to sell their services as guides to those passing through their lands.

Physical

Birdfolk stand slightly shorter than the average human, but weigh quite a bit less.

Their bones are strong but lightweight, and they are built lean and aerodynamic. Most birdfolk have faces resembling eagles or similar birds of prey, although there are many isolated tribes that resemble other birds, such as parrots, vultures, and crows.

A birdfolk’s hands are part of its wings—situated about midway along the outer edge, similar to the placement of the upper appendages of a bat or pterosaur. Birdfolk are able to use these hands as well as human hands, but only while they are not in flight. While flying, they cannot grasp anything with their hands and must leave them open—although they can use them to make gestures, such as for the somatic components of spells. A birdfolk can use the talons of its feet to grasp and carry items while it flies, but its feet are not dexterous enough to wield weapons or shields.

Birdfolk plumage varies. The birdfolk of the high mountains are known for their snow-white feathers and gray beaks, while those in the canyonlands have rust-red plumage with yellow-orange accents and black beaks.

Rarely, birdfolk make their home in completely different terrains, such as remote rainforest or redwood groves; they are said to have more brightly colored plumage.

Social

Most birdfolk prefer a simple existence spent in near-endless flight above their tribal territories, hunting for game, defending their lands from threats, and enjoying the wind beneath their wings. They spend their nights resting in open, partially-sheltered community nests, where they share equally in preparing meals, crafting, and singing. Few have any desire to leave this life, and even though they have potential for great mobility, few ever travel more than 100 miles from their place of birth.

Birdfolk see the world in terms of three dimensions. They think and move vertically, not just side-to-side, and so it pains them to be on the ground for very long at a time. In this respect, they see species without wings as being greatly disadvantaged. Birdfolk adventurers are rare, but usually have very strong motivations for leaving their life in the sky behind and allying themselves with ground-dwellers.

Alignment and Religion

Birdfolk are almost always Lawful, as they have a strong sense of community, tradition, and loyalty to their tribe. Most are Neutral, with some leaning toward Good, and only a few embracing Evil. There are many among them who embrace druidism, but most worship various gods of the air, sky, birds, or the weather. Some even directly worship one of the Elemental Lords of Air.

Names

Some typical birdfolk names include the following (choose or roll 1d12):

Aekiree
Arikia
Dreekaaha
Eerrah
Garakaa
Hanigaha
Heekakiree
Koriaha
Ooqui
Squaairra
Titachee
Weekikah
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are quick are perceptive, but slight of build. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Wis, –2 Str [standard]. (0)
Size Medium. As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type Humanoid. You are a Humanoid with the birdfolk subtype. (0)
Speed Slow. Your base speed is 20 feet. (–1)
Languages You begin play speaking Birdfolk and Auran. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Common, Draconic, Elven, and Sylvan. (0)
Other Species Traits
Claustrophobia Whenever you are in any kind of enclosed area (such as a building, underground tunnel, and so on) less than 15 feet wide in at least one direction (including vertically), you feel trapped and take a –2 penalty to saving throws against fear effects. If you have immunity to fear, that immunity is suppressed while you are under the effects of claustrophobia. (–1)
Flight You have wings that allow you to fly at a speed of 40 feet (poor maneuverability). You cannot fly while wearing medium or heavy armor, or while carrying a heavy load. (6)
Keen Eyesight Your distance vision is sharper than a human’s. You gain Eagle-Eyed as a bonus feat, even if you do not meet the prerequisites. (2)
Natural Armor You are surprisingly resilient and have a bony chest plate that affords a +1 natural armor bonus. (2)
Natural Weaponry While airborne, you can use your feet to make two talon attacks; these are primary natural attacks that deal 1d4 damage each. When grounded, you can use your beak to make a bite attack; this is a primary natural attack that deals 1d3 damage. You cannot use your talon and beak attacks in the same round. (2)
Total: 10 RP (standard)
Variants
Air Birdfolk

Some birdfolk aren’t native to the Material Plane at all. They hail from a world far removed from the solid earth that many birdfolk find so limiting, coming from the vast open skies of the Elemental Planes of Air itself. Those who call this plane home are natural scouts and explorers. Full of boundless enthusiasm, they consider themselves ambassadors of a world of endless sky and endless possibilities.

Sky-Born You gain the extraplanar subtype when you are not on the Elemental Planes of Air. You gain electricity resistance 5, and your species ability score modifiers are +4 Dex, –2 Str, –2 Int. This trait alters type and ability score modifiers and replaces natural armor.
Supple Wings Your maneuverability class improves from poor to good. (If you take the Improved Flight* feat, it improves by one additional step to perfect.) This trait alters flight and replaces natural weaponry.

Alternate Species Traits
Cooperative You gain a +2 bonus to skill checks for the aid another action and to attack rolls to aid another with a melee attack. A creature using the aid another action to assist you with a skill check gains a +2 bonus to their skill check. This trait replaces natural weaponry.
Ground-Walker You’ve spent a lot more time on the ground than most birdfolk. You’ve lost your awkwardness walking and your fear of enclosed spaces, but your wings are not as developed as most of your kin. Your base speed and your fly speed are both 30 feet, and your maneuverability class is clumsy. (If you take the Improved Flight* feat, your fly speed increases to 40 feet, and your maneuverability class improves to poor.) This trait alters your speed and flight, and replaces claustrophobia.
Javelin Hurler You have trained extensively and can use your talons to wield a single light or one-handed melee weapon while you are flying. (This weapon counts as being wielded in one hand, even if you use both talons to steady it.) Additionally, you can use your talons to throw javelins while flying. This trait replaces natural weaponry.
Nest Keeper You gain a +2 species bonus in any one Craft or Profession skill of your choice, and Craft and Profession are always class skills for you. This trait replaces keen eyesight.
Storm Caller Birdfolk sorcerers with the stormborn bloodline treat their Charisma score as 2 points higher for all sorcerer spells and class abilities. Birdfolk clerics with the Weather domain use their domain powers and spells at +1 caster level. This trait replaces keen eyesight.
Storm Watcher You gain a +2 species bonus to Knowledge (nature) checks, as well as a +2 species bonus to Survival checks to predict the weather. This trait replaces keen eyesight.
Species Feats
Dive Attack

While in flight, you can make a diving attack.

Prerequisites: Flyby Attack, birdfolk.

Benefit: A dive attack works like a charge, but you must move a minimum of 30 feet and descend at least 10 feet. You can make a dive attack only with your own talons, or with manufactured weapons that are able to wield with your talons. If the attack hits, double the weapon’s base damage.

Improved Flight

You become a stronger flier.

Prerequisites: Fly 5 ranks, birdfolk.

Benefit: Your fly speed increases by 10 feet, and your maneuverability improves by one step (for example, from poor to average).

Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add a +1/2 bonus to Fly checks and Perception checks while raging.
Bard Add one spell known from the bard spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level bard spell you can cast.
Bloodrager Add a +1/2 bonus to Fly checks and concentration checks while bloodraging.
Cleric Add a +1 bonus on caster level checks made to overcome the spell resistance of outsiders.
Druid Add a +1 bonus on wild empathy checks made to influence animals and magical beasts that have a natural fly speed.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a grapple or overrun while flying.
Hunter Add +1/3 to the number of minutes you can use animal focus each day.
Kineticist Add +1/3 point of damage to air element blasts that deal damage.
Oracle If you have the nature, wind, or elemental mystery, add one spell from the druid’s spell list that isn’t on the cleric spell list to your oracle spell list; you still must select this spell as one of your spells known in order to cast it. This spell must be at least one spell level lower than the highest-level oracle spell you can cast.
Ranger Add a +1/2 bonus on Perception checks made while flying or in a favored terrain.
Shaman Add a +1/2 bonus to Knowledge (nature) and Knowledge (planes) checks.
Skald Add one spell known from the skald spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level skald spell you can cast.
Sorcerer Choose a bloodline power from the djinni or elemental (air) bloodline that you can use. Treat your class level as though it were +1/6 higher (to a maximum of +2) when determining the effects of that power.
Spirit Warrior You gain electricity resistance 1 when you have an active aura. Each time this reward is selected, increase this electricity resistance by +1/2. This electricity resistance stacks with electricity resistance gained from other sources, including the shield aura.
Summoner Your eidolon gains resistance 1 against either electricity or sonic. Each time you select this reward, you increase your eidolon’s resistance to one of these energy types by 1 (maximum 10 for any one energy type).
Warpriest Add +1/2 to the number of times per day you can use blessings, but these additional uses can be from only the Air, Animal, Liberation, Tornado, and Weather blessings.
Witch Add one spell from the druid spell list to your familiar. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level witch spell you can cast. If your familiar is ever replaced, the new familiar knows these bonus spells.
Wizard Add +1/4 to your caster level when casting wizard spells with the air descriptor.
